correctness.rationale: Choose one color \(\alpha\) uniquely in the first part and a color \(\beta\) outside that part's palette uniquely in the second. For offset two, every second-part list has at least \(n_1+2\) colors; for offset one with at least three parts, the nonempty third part gives the same margin. Every later part can avoid all earlier colors because its list has at least \(N-n_i+1\) colors while at most \(N-n_i\) earlier vertices have been colored. Thus part palettes are disjoint, the coloring is proper, \(\beta\) uniquely witnesses every first-part vertex, \(\alpha\) uniquely witnesses every second-part vertex, and both are unique in every later neighborhood. Fresh arithmetic checks over every part-size profile with two through nine parts and sizes one through four reproduced every list-margin inequality.
